name: Hydrochloric Acid
description: A strong mineral acid widely used in laboratories, industry, and chemical analysis.
storage: Store in corrosion-resistant containers in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area away from bases.
first_aid: Flush affected area with water for at least 15 minutes and seek immediate medical attention.
disposal: Dispose of as hazardous waste according to local regulations after proper neutralization where appropriate.
green_alternative: Citric acid for suitable low-strength applications.
environmental_impact: Can significantly lower the pH of water bodies if released untreated.

name: Sulfuric Acid
description: A highly corrosive strong mineral acid used in laboratories, fertilizer production, and batteries.
storage: Store in acid-resistant containers away from water, bases, and organic materials.
first_aid: Immediately flush with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes and obtain medical attention.
disposal: Dispose of as hazardous waste following approved neutralization procedures.
environmental_impact: Can acidify soil and water, harming ecosystems.

name: Nitric Acid
description: A strong oxidizing acid commonly used in laboratories and fertilizer manufacturing.
storage: Store away from organic materials, reducing agents, and heat.
first_aid: Flush exposed areas with water for at least 15 minutes and seek emergency medical care.
disposal: Dispose through approved hazardous waste procedures.
green_alternative: Use less hazardous oxidizing agents where suitable.
environmental_impact: Can contribute to water pollution and acidification.

name: Acetic Acid
description: A weak organic acid commonly found in vinegar and laboratory applications.
storage: Store tightly sealed away from oxidizing agents.
first_aid: Wash exposed area thoroughly with water and seek medical advice if irritation persists.
disposal: Dispose according to laboratory chemical waste procedures.
green_alternative: Dilute vinegar for suitable educational demonstrations.
environmental_impact: Low environmental impact when properly handled.

name: Citric Acid
description: A naturally occurring weak organic acid widely used in green chemistry.
storage: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly closed container.
first_aid: Rinse eyes or skin with water if irritation occurs.
green_alternative: Already considered a green alternative for many acid applications.

name: Phosphoric Acid
description: A moderately strong acid used in laboratories, fertilizers, and food processing.
storage: Keep container tightly closed in a cool, ventilated area.
first_aid: Flush with water for at least 15 minutes if exposed.
disposal: Dispose according to hazardous waste guidelines.
green_alternative: Citric acid for mild cleaning applications.
environmental_impact: Excess release may contribute to algal blooms.

name: Formic Acid
description: A naturally occurring organic acid found in ant venom and used in laboratories.
storage: Store away from oxidizing agents and heat.
first_aid: Flush affected area with water and seek medical attention.
disposal: Dispose through approved hazardous waste disposal.
green_alternative: Use less hazardous organic acids when suitable.
environmental_impact: Can be harmful to aquatic life at high concentrations.

name: Oxalic Acid
description: An organic acid used in cleaning, bleaching, and laboratory applications.
storage: Store in a cool, dry location away from incompatible materials.
first_aid: Flush with water and obtain medical attention immediately.
green_alternative: Citric acid for light cleaning tasks.
environmental_impact: May affect aquatic organisms if improperly released.

name: Carbonic Acid
description: A weak acid formed when carbon dioxide dissolves in water.
disposal: Dispose according to local laboratory regulations.
green_alternative: Already environmentally friendly in most applications.
environmental_impact: Naturally present in many water systems.

name: Perchloric Acid
description: A very strong acid and powerful oxidizer requiring specialized handling.
storage: Store separately from combustible materials and reducing agents in approved containers.
first_aid: Flush with water immediately and seek emergency medical attention.
disposal: Dispose only through authorized hazardous waste procedures.
green_alternative: Use safer analytical reagents whenever possible.
environmental_impact: Can cause severe environmental contamination if released.
